decisions.reason: The 518 FLEX is a publicly rebranded version of an established, well-liked trommel screen, so both the investment and the visible commitment are high and dropping it within a year is unlikely.
The firm built a multi-model flail shredder line and presented it on its own page, so its public commitment and sunk development costs favour keeping it even if early sales are modest.

The mobile high-speed grinder line is only mentioned on the website, which signals lower visibility, but it is a multi-model investment that fits the firm's mobile processing strategy, so weak early results would likely be blamed on market ramp-up.
This single stationary electric fine shredder has low visibility and less sunk investment, but it fits the announced resource-saving, electric direction, so management would likely give it more time.
The green-waste grinder line serves core composting and biomass customers and involved several models, so management would persist despite its limited web presence.
The stationary pre-shredder line has its own page and supports the firm's push into tougher stationary processing, so the commitment is strong and it is very likely to stay.
